subject: Portfolio deep-dive: match vs replatform options
messages:
From: Leah Kim <leah@quartzhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Quentin Harris <quentin@quartzhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask — economics and migration risks

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for taking the time today. As promised, I wanted to summarize our current thinking so your team can help map practical options. We run critical inference for our customer support and clinical routing use cases — roughly 6M tokens/month today, bursty and latency-sensitive. We currently have a deal with CloudScale (contract thru June 2027) and they quoted a migration penalty and egress that together look like ~3 months of committed spend.

High-level asks:
- Can Redwood match the effective unit economics (including discounts) without a multi‑year commitment?
- If matching requires credits, how do you structure them so we don’t absorb one‑time egress costs?
- For customers who prefer replatforming (move models + infra), what would the realistic incremental engineering support look like and what credits do you typically offer for migration lift?

I’m attaching a small export of last 90 days usage and our current contract summary for reference.

Attaching: quartz_current_usage.csv, cloudscale-contract-summary.pdf

Appreciate any options you can share — Quentin and I will be making a recommendation to finance next week.

Best,
Leah
Leah Kim
Director, Platform Engineering
QuartzHealth
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Leah Kim <leah@quartzhealth.com>
Cc: Quentin Harris <quentin@quartzhealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — economics and migration risks

Leah — thanks for the detail and sending the usage file. Quick read-through notes below and a proposed plan to get you a quantifiable decision package by EOD Thursday.

Short answers up front:
- We can design a match-first offer (credits + stepped discounts) that neutralizes the net cost for 6–9 months while you validate perf in production. That option keeps you on your current runtime shape and limits engineering lift.
- Alternatively, a replatform pathway (move models to Redwood runtime + token-efficient quantized variants) typically requires a ~2–4 week tech integration effort for teams this size. We often combine a migration credit equal to 1–2 months of spend + a short-term committed discount to offset egress and migration support.

Proposed next steps (what I’ll deliver):
1) A concise matrix: match vs replatform (unit price, credits, estimated engineering days, risk level).
2) A sample SOW for a 2‑week pilot (scope: perf validation, KV cache tuning, canary routing).
3) A redlined commercial term that neutralizes CloudScale egress for the pilot period (if you share the egress line items).

I’ve pulled the first-pass matrix together — attaching redwood_match_vs_replatform_v1.xlsx. Connor, can you drop the pricing scenarios and a conservative credit table?

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Leah Kim <leah@quartzhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — economics and migration risks

Leah/Team — I pulled a conservative pricing pack based on the CSV and our standard migration philosophy. Key bullets:

- Match offer (low friction):
  * Effective token price: $0.0009/token (volume tier applied to current consumption profile)
  * One-time onboarding credit: $60k applied as a dollar credit to offset egress and first‑month delta (applies within 90 days)
  * No long-term commitment required; 60 day notice to cancel.

- Replatform offer (higher uplift, lower run cost):
  * Effective token price post-optimization: $0.0007/token (assumes quantized variants + batching optimizations)
  * Migration credit: equal to 1.5 months of historic spend (estimated $95k) to cover engineering time + egress; paid as credits over first 3 invoices
  * Technical onboarding: we include 16 hours of dedicated runtime engineering and a 2-week pilot SOW at no charge for the pilot period.

Risks & ops notes:
- If you need strict data residency and Private deployment, quotes shift +10–15% and we’d require an initial setup window.
- Egress documentation: we’ll need a line-item export to guarantee the credit fully covers CloudScale termination fees; without that we can only offer a cap.

Attachments: pilot-sow-draft.pdf (SOW outline), pricing-scenarios.csv (summary).

Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Leah Kim <leah@quartzhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Quentin Harris <quentin@quartzhealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 15:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — economics and migration risks

Soojin / Connor — appreciate the quick turnaround and the two clear pathways. A few clarifying points before we escalate to finance/legal: 

1) The egress line item is $72,400 per CloudScale termination schedule — I’ve attached the contract excerpt.
2) We prefer the replatform approach for long-term cost but need the migration credit to be guaranteed and tied to the pilot success criteria (latency within 15% of current 99th pct and no more than 2 regressions in NLU intent accuracy across our test set).
3) Can you show how the 1.5 month migration credit maps to our historic spend (I’ll attach the last 3 months invoice summary).

If Redwood can: (a) commit the $95k credit cap mapped to our invoices, (b) provide the free 2-week pilot SOW you attached, and (c) put the pilot terms in DocuSign so legal can review quickly, we’re prepared to recommend moving forward to procurement next week.

Next steps for us: I’ll attach the invoice extract and the contract excerpt (see attachments). Please send a DocuSign starter and we’ll queue legal review.

Best,
Leah
